scope: Image-only development inventory; no alignment scores or sound fitting
units: One visible peripheral human figure, excluding central zodiac emblem. Record head point and adjacent label anchor where visible. Coordinates approximate image locators, not segmentation truth. Do not force thirty figures.
geometry: Bands identified from drawn circular boundaries; extra-band figures form their own group. Order each circular band clockwise from image top. Extra top group ordered left-to-right, without claiming this is reading order. Candidate traversals later: bands radially inward versus outward, common CW versus CCW; extra group before versus after circular groups with left-right or right-left traversal. These alternatives must enter the full search correction. Split Aries/Taurus panel orders both retained. No per-sign tuning.
non30: If a sign has other than30 observed figures, exclude it from primary degree-by-degree alignment; retain descriptive inventory. Do not insert a gap, interpolate or choose omitted degree from fit. Any later gap model requires separate preregistration.
features: Torso garment clear / bare clear / ambiguous. Enclosing vessel clear / absent / ambiguous. Star visibly pigmented / unpainted / ambiguous. Clear means visible structure at inspected resolution; faintness is ambiguous, not absent. No inferred sex. Null accompanied by reason. Label point is association candidate, not a reading; absence requires visible empty space, otherwise unresolved.
null_requirements: Any future scoring must beat sign/panel/ring feature frequencies and ring-preserving cyclic shifts, with all searched orderings and correspondences corrected. No numeric alignment gate claimed frozen here.
independence: No glyph readings used. Same-agent annotation, not independent human labels. Earlier image familiarity and v83 exposure notes retained.
stop: Held-out signs remain unannotated and unscored. Finish image inventory before table values are consulted. Primary-source discovery may proceed, but do not read degree sequences during annotation.
